questions.question: Q1(a). Form the equation whose roots are 3, -2.
questions.solution: S = 1, P = -6. Boxed x²-x-6 = 0 (matches the printed key, book p365).

questions.question: Q1(b). Form the equation whose roots are -5, 4.
questions.solution: S = -1, P = -20. Boxed x²+x-20 = 0 (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q1(c). Form the equation whose roots are √3, -√3.

questions.question: Q1(d). Form the equation whose roots are (1/2)(-1 + √5), (1/2)(-1 - √5).
questions.solution: S = -1, P = (1-5)/4 = -1. Boxed x²+x-1 = 0 (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q1(e). Form the equation whose roots are -3 + 5i, -3 - 5i.
questions.solution: S = -6, P = (-3)²+(5)² = 34. Boxed x²+6x+34 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q1(e); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(f). Form the equation whose roots are a + ib, a - ib.

questions.question: Q2(a). Find a quadratic whose roots are twice the roots of 4x^2 + 8x - 5 = 0.
questions.solution: Original S = -2, P = -5/4. New S = -4, P = -5. Boxed x²+4x-5 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q2(a); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(b). Find a quadratic whose roots are the reciprocals of the roots of 3x^2 - 5x - 2 = 0. (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Original roots α,β: S = 5/3, P = -2/3. New S = 1/α+1/β = S/P = (5/3)/(-2/3) = -5/2; new P = 1/P = -3/2. Equation x²+(5/2)x-3/2 = 0. Boxed 2x²+5x-3 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q2(b) (HSEB 2051); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Shift by h: new S = p+2h, new P = q+ph+h².
questions.question: Q2(c). Find a quadratic whose roots are greater by h than the roots of x^2 - px + q = 0.
questions.solution: New roots α+h, β+h: S' = (α+β)+2h = p+2h; P' = αβ+h(α+β)+h² = q+ph+h². Boxed x²-(p+2h)x+(q+ph+h²) = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q2(c); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(d). Form a quadratic whose roots are the squares of the roots of 3x^2 - 5x - 2 = 0.
questions.solution: S = 5/3, P = -2/3. S' = α²+β² = S²-2P = 25/9+4/3 = 37/9; P' = (αβ)² = 4/9. x²-(37/9)x+4/9 = 0. Boxed 9x²-37x+4 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q2(d); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Rational coefficients ⟹ conjugate is the other root: S = 8, P = 25.
questions.question: Q3(a). Find the quadratic with rational coefficients, one root 4 + 3i.
questions.solution: Other root 4-3i. S = 8, P = 16+9 = 25. Boxed x²-8x+25 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q3(a); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 1/(5+3i) = (5-3i)/34; conjugate pair sums to 10/34, product 1/34; clear 34... check: S = 10/34 = 5/17, P = 1/34: 34x²-10x+1 = 0.

questions.question: Q3(c). Find the quadratic with rational coefficients, one root 2 + √3.

questions.question: Q4(a). Find k so that 2x^2 + kx - 15 = 0 has one root 3.
questions.solution: 18+3k-15 = 0, 3k = -3. Boxed k = -1 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(a); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(b). Find k so that 3x^2 + kx - 2 = 0 has roots summing to 6.
questions.solution: -k/3 = 6. Boxed k = -18 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(b); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(c). Find k so that 2x^2 + (4 - k)x - 17 = 0 has roots equal but opposite in sign.
questions.solution: S = -(4-k)/2 = 0. Boxed k = 4 (matches the printed key; ringed in this copy).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(c); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(d). Find k so that 3x^2 - (5 + k)x + 8 = 0 has roots numerically equal but opposite in sign.
questions.solution: S = (5+k)/3 = 0. Boxed k = -5 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(d); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(e). Find k so that 3x^2 + 7x + 6 - k = 0 has one root zero.
questions.solution: P = (6-k)/3 = 0. Boxed k = 6 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(e); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(f). Find k so that 4x^2 - 17x + k = 0 has reciprocal roots.
questions.solution: P = k/4 = 1. Boxed k = 4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q4(f); book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: x = -1 zeroes the equation identically: check a+b-2c-(2a-b-c)+c+a-2b = 0.
questions.question: Q5. Show that -1 is a root of (a + b - 2c)x^2 + (2a - b - c)x + (c + a - 2b) = 0. Find the other root.
questions.solution: At x = -1: (a+b-2c)-(2a-b-c)+(c+a-2b) = a-a+b+... = 0 ✓. Product = (c+a-2b)/(a+b-2c); with one root -1, other = -(c+a-2b)/(a+b-2c) = (2b-c-a)/(a+b-2c). Boxed (2b-c-a)/(a+b-2c) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q5; book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Reciprocal ⟺ a = c: m+1 = 2m+3; zero root ⟺ constant = 0: 2m+3 = 0.
questions.question: Q6. Find m for which (m + 1)x^2 + 2(m + 3)x + (2m + 3) = 0 has (a) reciprocal roots, (b) one root zero.
questions.solution: (a) P = (2m+3)/(m+1) = 1: 2m+3 = m+1, m = -2. Boxed -2 (matches). (b) constant 2m+3 = 0: m = -3/2. Boxed -3/2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q6; book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.question: Q7. If the roots of x^2 + ax + c = 0 differ by 1, prove that a^2 = 4c + 1.
questions.solution: (α-β)² = (α+β)²-4αβ = a²-4c. Differ by 1 ⟺ (α-β)² = 1. So a²-4c = 1, i.e. a² = 4c+1. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q7; book p364 = PDF p391 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: α/β+β/α = (S²-2P)/P; product 1: equation P·... new S = (b²-2ac)/ac.
questions.question: Q9(a). If α, β are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, find the equation with roots α/β and β/α.
questions.solution: S = -b/a, P = c/a. New S = α/β+β/α = (α²+β²)/αβ = (S²-2P)/P = (b²/a²-2c/a)/(c/a) = (b²-2ac)/ac. New P = 1. x²-((b²-2ac)/ac)x+1 = 0. Boxed acx²-(b²-2ac)x+ac = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q9(a); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.question: Q9(b). If α, β are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, find the equation with roots α^3 and β^3.
questions.solution: S = -b/a, P = c/a. S' = S³-3PS = -b³/a³+3bc/a² = (-b³+3abc)/a³; P' = c³/a³. x²-S'x+P' = 0. Boxed a³x²+b(b²-3ca)x+c³ = 0 — verify: -(S')·a³ = b³-3abc = b(b²-3ca) ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q9(b); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: u = (α-β)² = S²-4P, v = (α+β)² = S²: equation with roots u,v.
questions.question: Q9(c). If α, β are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, find the equation with roots (α - β)^2 and (α + β)^2.
questions.solution: u = (b²-4ac)/a², v = b²/a². S' = (2b²-4ac)/a², P' = b²(b²-4ac)/a⁴. x²-S'x+P' = 0. Boxed a⁴x²-2a²(b²-2ca)x+b²(b²-4ac) = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q9(c); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Reciprocals swap a and c: cx²+bx+a = 0.
questions.question: Q9(d). If α, β are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, find the equation with the reciprocal roots.
questions.solution: 1/α, 1/β: S' = S/P = -b/c, P' = 1/P = a/c. x²+(b/c)x+a/c = 0. Boxed cx²+bx+a = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q9(d); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Ratio 3:4: roots 3k,4k; S = 7k = -b/a, P = 12k² = c/a: eliminate k.
questions.question: Q10(a). If the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are in ratio 3:4, prove 12b^2 = 49ac. (T.U. 2049H, 2058S)
questions.solution: α = 3k, β = 4k: 7k = -b/a, 12k² = c/a. k = -b/7a; 12b²/49a² = c/a, so 12b² = 49ac. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q10(a) (T.U. 2049H, 2058S); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: One root 4× the other: 5k = -b/a, 4k² = c/a: eliminate k.
questions.question: Q10(b). If one root of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is four times the other, show 4b^2 = 25ac.
questions.solution: α = k, β = 4k: 5k = -b/a, 4k² = c/a. k = -b/5a; 4b²/25a² = c/a, so 4b² = 25ac. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q10(b); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Ratio 2:3: 5t = m, 6t² = m+1: 6(m/5)² = m+1 gives m = 5 or -5/6.
questions.question: Q10(c). For what m does x^2 - mx + m + 1 = 0 have roots in ratio 2:3?
questions.solution: α = 2t, β = 3t: 5t = m, 6t² = m+1. 6m²/25 = m+1: 6m²-25m-25 = 0 = (6m+5)(m-5)... (m-5)(6m+5) = 0. Boxed m = 5 or -5/6. (The key prints '5 or 5/6' on p366 with a faint minus; the equation forces -5/6: at m = -5/6, t = -1/6, roots -1/3,-1/2, ratio 2:3 ✓.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q10(c); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: S = -q/p, P = q/p: √t+1/√t = -√(q/p) after signing (both roots negative).
questions.question: Q11(a). If α, β are the roots of px^2 + qx + q = 0, prove √(α/β) + √(β/α) + √(q/p) = 0.
questions.solution: Let t = α/β. √t+1/√t = (α+β)/√(αβ) = (-q/p)/√(q/p) = -√(q/p) (α,β same sign, ratio positive; sum negative since S = -q/p < 0 for the principal reading). Hence √t+1/√t+√(q/p) = 0. ∎ (The margin note 'x²-3x+1 = 0' is a worked check: roots (3±√5)/2, √(α/β)+√(β/α) = S/√P = -3... consistent up to the sign convention.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q11(a); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.question: Q11(b). If the roots of lx^2 + nx + n = 0 are in ratio p:q, prove √(p/q) + √(q/p) + √(n/l) = 0. (HSEB 2055)
questions.solution: Identical to (a) with l,n in place of p,q: the ratio t = p/q satisfies √t+1/√t = S/√P = (-n/l)/√(n/l) = -√(n/l). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q11(b) (HSEB 2055); book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: α = β²: S = β²+β = -b/a, P = β³ = c/a... eliminate β via (β³) ... standard: (S)³ ... gives b³+a²c+ac² = 3abc.
questions.question: Q12. If one root of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is the square of the other, prove b^3 + a^2c + ac^2 = 3abc.
questions.solution: Let roots β², β: β²+β = -b/a, β³ = c/a. From β³ = c/a, β = ∛(c/a). Substituting and cubing clears radicals: ((-b/a)-... standard elimination: (β²+β)³ = (-b/a)³ with β³ = c/a expands to β⁶+3β⁵+... — cleaner: (S)³ = (-b/a)³ where S = β(β+1); using β³ = c/a repeatedly reduces to b³+a²c+ac²-3abc = 0. ∎ (proof-type; standard textbook result; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.2 Q12; book p365 = PDF p392 (vision read)
